notes: Adaptive semantic LLM mode enabled via TKNT_SEMANTIC_ADAPTIVE_LLM; deterministic stage fallbacks are disabled.
Kept canonical cluster ids and reduced to a compact full-function kitchen.
No new cluster added; inventory and room size support the canonical core plus optional island/hospitality only if surplus remains.
Tier hints are set for deterministic keep/drop selection with core items fixed and support items optional.
Kitchen is moderately sized with strong perimeter wall capacity and a clear circulation core, so core cooking/storage clusters should survive deterministic filtering.
Island support is viable only when surplus remains after core placement; prefer a compact island and keep it later than core items.
Hospitality items are nonessential for full kitchen functionality and should drop early unless the room has substantial surplus beyond core and island needs.
Active clusters mapped to kitchen function with longest-wall bias preserved.
Center openness kept clear for circulation; island remains optional-support if conflict arises.
Planner output is cluster/bundle/zone level only; pose is left to downstream composer and solver.
Style policy compiled before layout planning; downstream geometry treats it as bias, not a hard override.
Request contract attached before tier count so explicit functional objects are protected from silent pruning.
Tier Count used deterministic utility, capacity, and bundle-preserving rules, plus Forge semantic tier-count hints when available.
Tier Count itself did not run an additional LLM call.
Output is synchronized for the object-level anchor-first solver handoff.
Merged into solver-ready object program for object-level anchor-first placement.
Request contract is inferred from explicit brief object mentions; tier count may degrade but should not silently drop protected items.
